title: Kind Composition Matrix
purpose: Every kind guide in the dossier is written as if it's the only motion on the page. Real sites stack 3-5 kinds simultaneously. This file is what's missing: how they share budgets, what order they initialize in, and which pairs actively conflict.
source_authority: derived from 04_do_dont.md limits + 06_motion_grammar.md limit tokens + per-kind guide constraints; no single dossier file previously covered this

initialization_order.rule: engines that own the scroll/viewport must initialize before engines that read scroll position or viewport state

order.reason: preloader (if present) must resolve before anything else measures layout or starts a RAF loop; body.loading blocks scroll during this phase
Lenis must be constructed before ScrollTrigger.update is bound, and before any other kind reads window.scrollY
View Transitions API registration happens at route-change time, but the click-interceptor must be wired after Lenis exists so scroll position can be captured pre-transition

order.kind: kind-ii / kind-iii / kind-ix (whichever owns the full-viewport-scene slot)
order.reason: mount after the scroll engine so IntersectionObserver-driven pause logic has a stable scroll container to observe
registered after the full-viewport scene so its trigger boundaries don't get invalidated by a late-mounting canvas changing document height

order.kind: kind-iv, kind-v, kind-viii, kind-x, kind-xi, kind-xii
order.reason: inline/local kinds; mount order among these does not matter, but each MUST register its own cleanup independently

initialization_order.anti_pattern: mounting kind-ii/iii/ix before Lenis exists causes ScrollTrigger.refresh() to fire against a pre-scroll-engine document height, producing incorrect trigger boundaries that only surface after first scroll

conflict_pairs: kind-vi (only during its visible window, then releases)
kind-ii/iii/ix (only momentarily during the transition itself)
shared_budget_conflicts.resolution: kind-vi and kind-vii are transient consumers (they release the slot when done); kind-ii/iii/ix are the only kinds that hold the slot for the page's steady state. Router must reject a plan with more than one steady-state consumer.
shared_budget_conflicts.example_conflict: a product page wants a 3D hero (kind-ii) AND a shader background behind the pricing section (kind-iii) -> illegal. Resolve by making the shader a bounded-region canvas (not full-viewport) so it falls outside this budget, or by dropping one.

shared_budget_conflicts.resolution: sum ALL currently-looping ambient elements across every active kind, not per-kind. A shader background (1 loop) + a looping Lottie icon in the nav (1 loop) already uses the full budget of 2 -- a second looping Lottie elsewhere on the same viewport is a violation.
shared_budget_conflicts.example_conflict: kind-iii ambient shader + kind-x audio visualizer + kind-v looping onboarding animation, all visible in the same viewport at once = 3 loops, exceeds cap. Stagger visibility (pause off-screen loops via IntersectionObserver) or cut one.

conflict_pairs: all kinds contribute to this shared pool simultaneously
shared_budget_conflicts.resolution: count every simultaneously-animating element in the current viewport at any single timestamp, across all active kinds combined, not per-kind. A hero with 3 kind-i staggered reveals + 4 kind-viii hover-ready cards + 1 kind-iv cursor follower can hit 8 easily if the user hovers while scrolling.
shared_budget_conflicts.example_conflict: kind-i staggered card grid (6 cards revealing) fires at the same scroll position where kind-viii hover states are also active on already-revealed cards above the fold -- can exceed 8 concurrent tracks. Stagger kind-i reveals with motion.delay.item so the peak concurrent count stays under budget, and profile with Playwright's animation-count assertion (see kind-i.spec.ts pattern) at the worst-case scroll position, not just at rest.

known_engine_conflicts.conflict: both try to own scroll position interpolation; user sees jittery double-easing
known_engine_conflicts.resolution: set scroll-behavior: auto globally when Lenis is active; never set both (04_do_dont.md Avoid #8)

known_engine_conflicts.conflict: both intercept navigation and animate the route change; double-fires if both are wired to the same click handler
known_engine_conflicts.resolution: feature-detect once at the router level: if 'startViewTransition' in document, use only the native API; Swup/Barba is the fallback branch, never both active simultaneously

pair: kind-x audio visualizer both reading pointermove/RAF on the same page
known_engine_conflicts.conflict: each kind's guide shows its own RAF loop; naive composition produces N independent RAF loops instead of one shared tick
known_engine_conflicts.resolution: starter scaffolds should expose one shared RAF ticker (see lib/scroll-setup.ts's gsap.ticker pattern) that all kinds subscribe to, rather than each kind calling its own requestAnimationFrame

known_engine_conflicts.conflict: two separate WebGL contexts on one page can exceed the browser's per-page context limit (typically 8-16) and silently fail
known_engine_conflicts.resolution: if both kind-ii and kind-iii are needed, they should share ONE Three.js renderer/scene rather than instantiate independently -- this is also why they share the full-viewport-scenes budget above

agent_instruction: Before generating code for a multi-kind page, run the router's ordered_kind_list through shared_budget_conflicts. If any conflict_pair is fully present in the list AND both are steady-state (not transient) consumers, stop and surface the conflict rather than generating code that will silently violate the token limits at runtime.
